Shopify vs WordPress vs Squarespace: Which Fits Your Small Business

By Marie Glow StudioPublished October 23, 2026

Shopify, WordPress and Squarespace solve different problems: Shopify is built to sell products and handle checkout, Squarespace gets a simple site live fast with no code, and WordPress offers the most flexibility and the deepest control over SEO. The right one depends on whether you are selling products, booking services, or publishing content, not which platform is trendiest.

What Does Each Platform Actually Do Best?

Shopify, WordPress and Squarespace are built for different jobs, so a head to head comparison only means something once you know which job you need done. Shopify is a hosted platform built specifically to sell products online, with the cart, checkout, inventory and shipping rules built in. Squarespace is a hosted, template based builder designed to get a clean site live quickly without writing code, which suits a portfolio, a simple business page or a service page better than a store with a growing product catalog. WordPress is open source software you or a host install and run, and its real strength is depth: a wide ecosystem of plugins and themes lets it do almost anything, including the content heavy, SEO focused site a blog or a publishing business needs.

What each platform is actually built for
PlatformBuilt forCoding needed to run it
ShopifySelling products, with checkout and inventory built inNone for day to day use
SquarespaceGetting a simple site live fast, with no store or a small oneNone
WordPressContent heavy sites, blogs and deep SEO controlHelpful, though themes and plugins reduce how much you need

Is Shopify the Right Starting Point for a Product Business?

Shopify is usually the right starting point for a product business because it is built around selling rather than publishing. A shop owner with physical or digital products gets a cart, checkout, inventory tracking and shipping rules that already work together, instead of a stack of plugins pieced together to do the same job. That matters most once a catalog grows past a handful of items, since Shopify is built to keep variants, stock levels and order flow organized as it grows. A service business rarely needs any of this, which is the clearest sign Shopify is not the automatic answer for every small business, only for the ones with something to check out.

When Is Squarespace Enough for a Small Business?

Squarespace is enough when a business needs one clean, professional presence online fast, with no store to manage or only a handful of items to sell. A coach, a consultant, a salon or a contractor who mainly needs a page that explains the service, shows the work and gives a way to book a call, request a quote or make a phone call often does not need Shopify’s full commerce engine or WordPress’s plugin ecosystem. The tradeoff is flexibility: templates keep setup simple, which also means less room to customize structure or add deeper SEO controls later without starting to outgrow the platform.

Why Would a Business Choose WordPress Instead?

A business chooses WordPress when it needs more control over structure and SEO than a template based builder allows, usually because content is doing real work: a blog with dozens of posts, a resource library, or a site that needs specific schema markup, custom layouts or detailed internal linking between pages. That flexibility comes from installing and maintaining plugins and themes yourself, or paying someone to, which is more ongoing setup than Squarespace and a different kind of work than running a Shopify store.

What About a Custom Coded Site Instead of Any of the Three?

A fourth option exists for a service business that does not need an online store or a content heavy blog: a custom coded site built around one job, like getting a call booked, a quote requested or a form filled out. Web design and development at Marie Glow Studio builds two kinds of sites for exactly this reason: Shopify for a product business that needs to sell, and a custom coded site for a service business that needs to get chosen, with no monthly platform fee and little to maintain beyond hosting. Neither WordPress nor Squarespace is part of that lineup, because the decision is made on what the business needs the site to do, not on which platform happens to be familiar.

How Should You Actually Decide Between Them?

The decision gets simpler once it is tied to the one job the site needs to do, not to which platform a friend used or which one looked easiest in a demo.

  • Selling products, with a cart and checkout to manage: Shopify
  • A simple service or portfolio presence, with no store, built fast: Squarespace
  • A content heavy site that needs deep SEO and structural control: WordPress
  • A service business that mainly needs a booking link, a quote form or a phone number to work: a custom coded site built around that one job

Whichever platform fits the job, the site still has to earn its keep: a visitor needs to land on a page that answers their question and gives them a clear next step, not just a platform that is technically set up. That is the real test behind small business website essentials and behind weighing a DIY website against a professionally designed one, regardless of which platform ends up underneath it.

If none of the three feels like the right fit, or an existing site on one of them still is not converting, the Website Starter is a one page, professionally designed site built around a shop or a service, typically ready in about a business week once intake is complete.

Frequently asked questions

Is Shopify always the best choice for a small business website?

No. Shopify is built to sell products, so it fits a product business well. A service business with no store to manage, such as a salon, a contractor or a coach, often does better with a simple site or a custom coded one built around booking a call or requesting a quote.

Does Marie Glow Studio build websites on WordPress or Squarespace?

No. Marie Glow Studio builds on Shopify for a product business that needs to sell, and builds a custom coded site for a service business that needs to get chosen. The business decides the platform, not a preference for one tool over another.

What is the fastest way to get a professional site live without picking a platform myself?
